title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-liam-brown
content:
Personal scratchpad for common clauses to watch and quick negotiation talking points (for sales + AE prep). Informal notes - keep concise.

Top priorities / red flags:
- Indemnity / liability cap: always push to financial cap = fees paid in last 12 months OR fixed $1M (whichever is lower) for standard customers. For enterprise with strong negotiating leverage, consider higher but insist on reciprocal indemnity.
  - Watch for unlimited liability carve-outs (e.g., IP claims) - narrow to direct IP infringement only. Avoid open-ended gross negligence carve-outs.
- Exclusion of consequential damages: ensure broad exclusion is preserved; customer will ask to carve out for breach of confidentiality and IP claims - allow only for those narrow categories.
- IP & ownership of outputs: we do NOT assign underlying model/IP. For customer-specific outputs: grant them a limited license to use outputs for their internal business purposes; avoid language implying transfer of model weights or ownership of model improvements.
- Data usage / training: no training on customer data without express opt-in. If they demand training rights, trade for higher price / longer term or explicit anonymization & limited retention.
- Confidentiality: tighten definition of confidential info to exclude publicly known, independently developed, or information required to be disclosed by law. Add clear data handling for PII.
- Security / compliance commitments: accept SOC2 Type II, ISO where we have it. Resist pushing for high-cost certifications if not in scope. For private deployments, can accept additional controls but list as SOW/Professional Services.
- Data residency: if customer requires EU/UK residency, consider Dedicated or Private offering. For hosted standard, provide region-based hosting options and delete-on-termination assurances.
- Breach notification: require 72 hours notice if realistically possible; try to keep to 72-96 hours. For large breaches, require immediate notice + remediation plan.
- Audit rights: limit to once per year, reasonable scope, and require notice + mutually agreed vendor-friendly auditor (redact sensitive trade secrets). Prefer remote-only audits where possible.
- Termination & transition assistance: define termination assistance at a daily rate or capped fee for exports and migration; include minimum notice (30-90 days) and deliverables.
- SLA / credits: standard is 99.9% for hosted API; define credit schedule and cap. Avoid customers asking to convert credits into termination rights.

AI-specific clauses:
- Model output risk / hallucinations: include explicit disclaimer that we are not liable for outputs and customer is responsible for downstream use. If customer insists, limit remedies to credits only.
- Output ownership: customer owns outputs but we reserve right to use de-identified telemetry for model improvement unless they opt out. Offer an opt-out (paid feature) for training prohibition.
- Reverse-engineering: prohibit customer from reverse-engineering curated model artifacts or runtime.
- Model improvements: if customer contributes proprietary prompts/data that materially improve our model, clarify whether that becomes part of our models - lean toward company owning improvements but offer license back to customer if significant.

Clause-by-clause quick notes (common redlines):
- Definitions: check "Customer Data" vs "Feedback" vs "Derived Data" - ensure clear boundaries and deletion obligations.
- Confidentiality duration: standard 3 years post-term; for trade secrets, survive indefinitely.
- Warranty: limit to 'conforms materially to documentation' + hygiene warranty (no deliberate backdoors). Avoid broad guarantees on accuracy of outputs.
- Indemnity: customers often want vendor to indemnify for third-party IP claims resulting from model outputs - accept only if customer provides indemnity for misuse and we retain control over model updates.
- Subprocessors/subcontractors: we should allow subprocessors but require notice and a right to object for critical vendors. Keep flow-down obligations limited to same security standards.

Negotiation talking points to hand to AE/AM:
- If customer pushes for lower liability cap: propose a middle ground (fees last 12 months + insurance threshold). Highlight sector risk (health/finance) to justify higher cap or Private mode.
- Data training demand: "We can agree to limited training rights under a paid addendum - includes anonymization, retention limits, and retraction rights."
- SLA demands beyond 99.9%: suggest Dedicated offering with SLA-backed credits and optional Premium Support add-on.
- Excessive audit requests: offer a quarterly compliance report + one annual third-party audit instead of ad-hoc full audits.

Redline language snippets (for quick paste):
- Liability cap: "Except for liability arising from (i) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) breach of confidentiality, or (iii) infringement of third-party intellectual property, each party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the total amount paid or payable by Customer to Vendor under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim."
- Data usage: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data to train or improve Vendor's models except with Customer's prior written consent. Vendor may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry for operational improvement provided such data cannot reasonably be re-identified to Customer."
- Termination assistance: "Upon termination for any reason, Vendor will provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of sixty (60) days at Vendor's then-current professional services rates and will export Customer Data in a commonly used format."

Unresolved questions / items to follow up:
- Check with infra team on expected region-level residency options for EU customers (timeline + cost). (Ticket: LEGAL-238)
- Confirm SOC2 renewal date and scope - need to provide evidence for enterprise buyer next week.
- Pricing playbook for customers who demand 'no-training' clause - propose 20%-40% uplift depending on data sensitivity.

Quick checklist before sending final redline to customer:
[ ] Confirm last 12 months spend for liability cap calculation
[ ] Add explicit data deletion timeframe post-termination (30/60/90 days)
[ ] Ensure breach notification timeline included and contact points
[ ] Attach security documentation (SOC2 / pen-test summary)
[ ] Add opt-out paid addendum language for training rights

Notes to self: keep communications pragmatic and solution-oriented. Offer product alternatives (Dedicated/Private) where legal asks are unreasonable for hosted. Use PS/SOW to capture one-off commitments. Save common snippets in contract-clauses library.

End of scratchpad.
